taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a shrub (FEIS, Anderson 2001).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: most plants 0.5 m to 2 m high, inside FEIS's 0.3 m to 2.7 m.

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "obtaining a height of 1 to 9 feet (0.30-2.7 m)"; Abrams (1951 p. 667): a straggly shrub up to 3 m high.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "a native desert shrub".

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "spiny, rounded, and much branched" shrub.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "This species is drought deciduous, meaning it loses foliage in response to low moisture availability".

traits.rosette.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "rounded, and much branched", leafy along the twigs: no rosette.

traits.spines.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "spines are numerous and slender, 0.20 to 0.80 inch (5-20 mm) long".

traits.twig_colour.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "Twigs are light barked"; sRGB by eye from the photos (pale grey).

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves alternate, often clustered on short spurs, as in the genus.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves linear-terete to narrowly oblanceolate: simple.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves entire, succulent.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves 3-15 mm. long (FEIS: 3-17 mm).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves succulent, 1-3 mm. broad.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves linear-terete to narrowly oblanceolate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: leaves entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves glabrous and fleshy.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flowers borne singly or two together along the twigs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 38852659, 141752536, 71578132, 7864093, 402609099, 21422212, 89733889, 39435825): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flowers along the twigs in the leaf clusters, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 38852659, 141752536, 71578132, 7864093, 402609099, 21422212, 89733889, 39435825): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: corolla whitish suffused with lavender; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 788): ochroleucous with pale lavender lobes. sRGB by eye.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: corolla tube 10-16 mm. long, the lobes short: tubular.

traits.corolla_tube_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: corolla tube 10-16 mm. long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: corolla lobes 1.5-2.5 mm. long, the open mouth 5 to 8 mm across.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: corolla lobes 4-5.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: stamens exserted 2-3 mm.

traits.fruit_type.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 788), Lycium: fruit a berry.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: fruit ovoid-ellipsoid.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: fruit bright red, 4-8 mm. long.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 667, Lycium andersonii: fruit bright red; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 788): scarlet. sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 789), Lycium andersonii: up to 5,600 feet, February to April (and August and September after summer rain); Abrams (1951 p. 667): March to May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: berries ripe in April and May, before the plant goes dormant in late May (FEIS).

traits.elevation_min_m.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): on washes, flats, mesas and slopes "generally from 1,500 to 6,000 feet (457-1,829 m) in elevation".

traits.elevation_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "generally from 1,500 to 6,000 feet (457-1,829 m) in elevation"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 789): up to 5,600 feet.

traits.light.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): "commonly grows on sandy or gravelly washes, sandy or alkali flats, mesas and slopes".

traits.moisture.note: FEIS species review, Lycium andersonii (Tesky 1992): on sites with about 128 to 162 mm of annual precipitation.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a rounded, much-branched shrub of pale grey spiny twigs, clusters of small fleshy green leaves, pale lavender-white tubular flowers and bright red berries in spring.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Anderson's wolfberry from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of snowbrush ceanothus (ceanothus-velutinus); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.2 m tall at 15 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
